title: External processors: establish provenance before execution
goal: Make a justified admission decision without executing unknown code.
prerequisites: 1c-enterprise.a 6; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
outcomes: Use the standard report instead of unknown repair code.
sections: An external processor can read/change data, access files and use available platform actions. Its extension does not make it safe; nor does a familiar sender prove unchanged content. Establish author, purpose, official source and required rights before opening anything. Never execute an unknown file out of curiosity.

EPF denotes an external data processor and ERF an external report. They can contain executable BSL; an extension is not a trust mark. This beginner course requires no “repair everything” processor: use standard cards/reports. Do not open unknown code merely to observe its behavior.
A hash binds review to a file

SHA256 binds a reviewed copy to later bytes; it does not itself prove harmlessness. A malicious file also has a hash. Compare against a trusted channel and attach review to that exact copy. Any modification creates new bytes requiring a new review.

An admission record identifies author/source, purpose, exact version, SHA256, expected reads/writes and reviewed environment. A hash binds review to bytes but does not establish safety. A changed file needs renewed review. An infobase copy protects source records, not arbitrary computer files or network access.
An infobase copy does not isolate the computer

A copy protects source records from ordinary mistakes but does not confine code to that directory. A test infobase is not permission to run unknown BSL on the main computer. Safe mode and rights have specific contexts; full execution isolation requires an agreed boundary and evidence, not a checkbox.

Compare “show my request total” with “repair everything by disabling checks.” The first uses the existing report. The second needs a defined algorithm, scope and admission. Do not change security settings to make a file run. Sandbox is an optional engineering tool, not a required step in learning installed 1C.

Without a trusted source and approved environment, the outcome isNOTRUN with a reason and specialist request. That is a correct decision, not a learning failure. Practice with original teaching source and predicted actions. Execute only after admission, on synthetic data, with before/after state checks and bounded output.

This lab produces a review record and NOT RUN for an unknown file. That is a valid negative outcome, not simulated execution. A known own processor needs separate source, reproducible build and an authorized synthetic-data test, developed in the programming course. Do not publish third-party configurations or real records.

lab.title: External processors: establish provenance before execution
lab.environment: Own continuing service-desk copy; no real data. Studio/Sandbox optional.
steps: Specify the need for one customer total and whether the standard report covers it.
Filter your customer and reconcile source numbers/minutes. Open no new external file.
For a fictional unknownEPF list missing provenance/source/version/permission scope. Treat any hash only as byte identity.
State NOT RUN, reason, required review and safe alternative. Keep protection enabled; do not run the file to test rejection.
Retain report parameters and admission record. Course completion does not establish safeEPF execution.
evidence: Actual settings/identities, expected and observed results, before/after work preserved.
For unexecuted code or future behavior, explicit NOT RUN/PLANNED instead of a native PASS.
lab.negative: NOT RUN: a hash proves neither content safety nor permission.

mistakes: A known hash is treated as a safety guarantee.
Bind bytes to review and separately assess author/code/permissions/environment.
An infobase copy is treated as whole-computer isolation.
Separate database preservation from executable system access.
Unknown code is run to prove that it should be refused.
Decide NOT RUN before execution and use the standard route.
